subtype: Approach: pushing it off until just before bedtime [Pitfall]
passage: At the hostel study hour, Dev told himself there was plenty of time. He played cricket in the corridor with a rolled-up sock and watched cartoons in the common room. When the 9 o'clock bell rang, he opened his science file and saw the diagram of the digestive system. It would take an hour. His stomach dropped. Tears came, and he walked to the warden's room. "Bidisha Ma'am, I have not started." Bidisha sat with him, helped him see where to begin, and stayed while he drew the first outline. Lights out came before the labels were done.

qa.q: What was Dev doing instead of homework during study hour?
qa.a: He played cricket in the corridor and watched cartoons.

qa.q: What was Dev feeling when he opened the science file at 9 o'clock?
qa.a: He felt panicked and sad. His stomach dropped, tears came, and he went to the warden for help.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Dev use another evening, and why?
qa.a: He could look at his homework first and put the longest task at the start. Then he would know how much time it really needs.

qa.q: How does Bidisha see Dev arriving at her room at that hour?
qa.a: Bidisha sees a child who is upset, not lazy, and who chose to ask for help. Bidisha sits with him while he begins.

grounding: A boy tells himself there is plenty of time, plays until 9 pm, then finds the diagram takes an hour, cries and asks an adult to help.

subtype: Approach: pushing it off until just before bedtime [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Charu, and I share a room with my brother Chetan, so I saw the whole thing. After school he said, "Science is only one diagram, I've got loads of time," and went to play cricket in the lane till dark. Then cartoons, then dinner, then more cartoons. At nine he opened his notebook and read the question: draw and label the human digestive system. He counted the labels. Fourteen. His face crumpled and he started crying. "Papa, it'll take an hour!" Papa came and sat with him, yawning, sharpening pencils while Chetan drew. I can't say what Chetan was thinking earlier, but at nine he didn't look like he had loads of time.

qa.q: How many labels did the diagram need?
What was Chetan feeling at nine when he read the question?
qa.a: His face crumpled and he cried, so he felt panicked and upset, realising the diagram would take an hour.

qa.q: What could Chetan do differently tomorrow?
qa.a: Look at the homework right after school and do the diagram before cricket, since 'loads of time' vanished once he started playing.

qa.q: What is it like for Papa at nine o'clock?
qa.a: Papa is tired and yawning but still sits and helps, so Chetan's delay has become Papa's late night too.

grounding: Shows a boy telling himself there is plenty of time, playing and watching cartoons, then crying at nine when the diagram needs an hour.

subtype: Approach: pushing it off until just before bedtime [Pitfall]
passage:
Friday. Dhruv's teacher set one weekend task: a labelled diagram of a plant cell. "Two whole days," Dhruv told Kalyani, his mother, and dropped his bag by the door.
Saturday. Cricket in the society park till lunch, cartoons till dinner, then more cricket on the terrace. The bag stayed by the door.
Sunday, 9 pm. Dhruv finally opened the textbook. The cell had eleven parts, and each needed a label and a colour. He did the maths: at least an hour. His chin shook, and then he was sobbing. "Amma, help me, please!" Kalyani sighed, switched off the TV and pulled up a chair.

qa.a: A labelled diagram of a plant cell.

qa.q: Why was Dhruv sobbing on Sunday night?
qa.a: He felt panicked and overwhelmed when he saw eleven parts needing at least an hour, so late on Sunday.

qa.q: What would have helped on Saturday?
qa.a: Doing the diagram before cricket in the park; 'two whole days' felt like plenty, but it disappeared without a plan.

qa.q: How might Kalyani see Sunday night?
qa.a: Kalyani sighs and switches off the TV, so she seems tired and a bit frustrated, but still chooses to sit with him.

grounding: Illustrates a boy believing he has plenty of time all weekend, then crying at 9 pm on Sunday when the diagram needs an hour.
